claims.reason: This is an argument of the theorem. It is instance-implicit and its type mentions only `X`, which is already an argument because `b : X → X` appears in the statement and `hb` is pulled in by `include`. Nothing in the statement `Function.Injective b` needs it. The proof works for any type: `congrArg (fun z => b (b z)) h` gives `b (b (b x)) = b (b (b y))`, and `simpa [hb]` rewrites this to `x = y`. Finiteness is never used, so `omit [Fintype X] in` would leave the theorem and its proof valid.
